description:
✨ Join Women and Gender eXpansive Coders DC (WGXC DC) online as we craft-n-crush our coding interviews. We’ll be taking crafting breaks in between trying out coding interview problems.

Not sure what craft to bring? Any creative outlet counts, be it a coloring book from your favorite TV show, that scarf you’ve been knitting for 5 years, or poems on the back of your fast food receipt. No judgment.

Need to practice for a coding interview? ✍🏾 Any company that hires for technical roles (e.g. software engineers, data analysts) may use coding interviews. You may be sent a timed 30 minute quiz, or you may need to solve a problem in real-time with your interviewer on a video call.
Example coding interview question from LeetCode: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

How am I going to craft and code at the same time? We’ll be taking crafting breaks in between trying out coding interview problems. The format we’ll be trying out is:

* ✍🏾 Part A (\~15 minutes): try to solve the given problem on your own
* 🧑‍💻 Part B (\~15 minutes): discuss the solution together with other attendees, time to ask questions and review our approach
* 🧶 Part C (\~15 minutes): crafting together, open conversation / networking / music
* Repeat ✍🏾, 🧑‍💻, 🧶 until time’s up.

✅ Why you should attend:

* Relax and reduce anxiety by practicing a creative hobby
* Make new friends
* Improve your coding interview skills
* Build your network of technologists in the DMV area

**This event is primarily intended to create an empowering and supportive space for women and non-binary individuals to find community, learn new technical concepts, and expand their coding and technical skills. description:
Every postmortem asks what went wrong during the response. What often gets missed is the foundation that was already there before the page fired: the ownership, the runbook, the last deploy. We'll follow one incident from page to postmortem, then go back to the platform work that made it possible, including how to use AI to augment incident response.

We'll cover:
- What good looks like end-to-end: one incident from page to postmortem, investigated, remediated, and documented in one place
- The foundation underneath it: ownership and on-call in the service catalog, runbooks and dependencies attached, readiness tracked on scorecards
- Where AI actually augments the response, from catching responders up to drafting the postmortem, and the platform data it needs to do it

name: Introducing the IPRAM Lab for Tokenized Regulated Asset Markets
description:
The tokenisation of regulated real-world assets has led to multiple institutional implementations of the same financial instruments, each operating on its own infrastructure with few shared patterns for how those infrastructures interoperate. As a result, tokenised assets remain confined to the environment they were issued in, accessible only to counterparties already inside the same institutional perimeter.

The IPRAM Lab ([https://github.com/LFDT-IPRAM](https://github.com/LFDT-IPRAM)) develops open implementation patterns for the interoperation of tokenised real-world regulated financial assets and the markets they participate in. This session introduces the lab's mission, scope, and the initial interoperability challenges it aims to address. All interested parties are invited to join!

name: VeltoraCore - The Optimization Layer for Fragmented Markets
description:
Join us for a discussion about the new VeltoraCore lab that is building a pair-coin, system-agnostic optimization engine that jointly coordinates user execution and LP participation in a single feasibility framework. A lightweight Proof-of-Optimization (PoO) mechanism cryptographically commits optimized batch outcomes to external system states, enabling verifiable cross-system settlement. Simulations on the ETH–USD pair show superior retained execution and materially lower user fees relative to benchmarks, while delivering liquidity-provider returns higher with reduced volatility.

This is a great opportunity to talk to the developers about what they're building and to learn how to get involved if this sounds interesting.

More about the VeltoraCore lab is at: [https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/veltoracore](https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/veltoracore)

name: Enterprise AI infrastructure in 2026: A reality check for platform engineers
description:
After two years of hype, many enterprises feel they’ve overspent on AI infrastructure without realizing the promised value.
In this session, Dan Ciruli, Kelsey Hightower, and Luca Galante cut through the buzzwords to show what enterprise AI infrastructure actually looks like in production.

In most cases, it is often less about training models from scratch and more about how platform engineering teams can fold AI inference and fine-tuning directly into their existing infrastructure.

**Join the discussion to learn:**
1. Why you don’t need infrastructure for training models from scratch, and how to start treating inference and fine-tuning just like serving standard web APIs.
2. Strategies for folding AI workloads and autonomous agents into your existing heterogeneous environments (VMs + containers + legacy databases) without rebuilding everything.
3. How to build an Agentic Development Platform (ADP) based on actionable reference architectures to deploy real-world AI applications.
